message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but their evolutionary history is quite unique. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) diverged from other bear lineages around 19–20 million years ago during the Miocene epoch. Fossil evidence suggests that early ancestors were omnivorous and adapted to forested environments. Over time, they evolved specialized traits—such as a pseudo-thumb formed from an enlarged wrist bone—to help them manipulate bamboo, which now constitutes the bulk of their diet. Their closest living relatives are the red panda (Ailurus fulgens), which split off earlier, around 25–30 million years ago. This lineage shows how diverse the bear family has been in adapting to various ecological niches.
